Title: Untitled Report

Data Analysis  
Conducted analysis of collected data to identify trends and insights relevant to the project objectives.

Data Collection  
Engaged in the collection of necessary data from various sources to support ongoing analysis and reporting efforts.

Report Presentation  
Prepared and organized the presentation of findings to ensure clarity and effective communication of results to stakeholders.
reports.content:
**Title: Untitled Report**

**Data Analysis**  
Conducted a thorough and systematic analysis of the collected data, employing a diverse array of statistical methods and analytical tools, such as regression analysis, cluster analysis, and time-series forecasting, to uncover significant trends and insights that are directly aligned with the project objectives. This comprehensive analysis involved identifying patterns over time, examining correlations between different data sets, and detecting any anomalies that may warrant further investigation. Each finding was meticulously documented, providing a detailed account of the implications for the project, which will serve to inform strategic decision-making processes. Additionally, the analysis included a comparative review of historical data to contextualize current findings and enhance the overall understanding of the project's landscape.

**Data Collection**  
Engaged in a comprehensive and methodical approach to the collection of essential data from a wide range of diverse sources, including structured surveys, in-depth interviews, and existing databases. This multi-faceted data collection strategy was designed to ensure that all relevant information was captured, thereby supporting ongoing analysis and reporting efforts. Special attention was given to the accuracy and reliability of the data, with rigorous validation processes implemented, such as cross-referencing with secondary sources and employing data cleaning techniques, to enhance the integrity of the findings. The collection process was also designed to be inclusive, ensuring that a broad spectrum of perspectives was represented, which is critical for a holistic understanding of the project context.

**Report Presentation**  
Prepared and meticulously organized the presentation of findings, utilizing a variety of visual aids such as charts, graphs, and infographics to enhance clarity and facilitate the effective communication of results to stakeholders. The presentation was structured to highlight key insights and actionable recommendations, ensuring that complex information was conveyed in an accessible manner. Each section of the presentation was crafted to build upon the previous one, guiding stakeholders through the narrative of the data. Feedback from stakeholders was actively sought during the presentation to foster a collaborative environment and to address any questions or concerns that arose, ensuring that all voices were heard and considered in the final reporting. Follow-up sessions were also scheduled to delve deeper into specific areas of interest, further enriching the dialogue surrounding the findings.

reports.content:
**WEEK 1 REPORT SUMMARY**

This report outlines the activities from the first week of field practice in Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E). Key activities included:

1. **Review of M&E Frameworks**: Analyzed current M&E practices to identify improvement areas, such as data collection gaps and reporting inconsistencies.

2. **Data Collection**: Engaged in various data collection methods (surveys, interviews, focus groups) to gather comprehensive information for projects, ensuring ethical standards were met.

3. **Stakeholder Engagement**: Held discussions with stakeholders to understand their M&E needs and challenges, integrating their insights into future planning.

4. **Development of SMART Indicators**: Collaborated with project teams to create Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound indicators for tracking progress and accountability.

5. **Daily Field Reporting**: Prepared daily reports summarizing activities, findings, and reflections, supporting transparency and continuous improvement in M&E strategies.

**Weekly Report**

**Title:** Untitled Report

**Introduction:**  
This report summarizes the activities and findings from the past week as part of my field practice in the Department of Health Systems Management. The focus has been on monitoring and evaluation practices, data management, and collaboration with various stakeholders.

**Activities Summary:**

1. I conducted a review of existing monitoring and evaluation frameworks in place at the host organization to assess their effectiveness and identify areas for improvement.

2. I participated in a training session on data management techniques, which enhanced my understanding of data collection, analysis, and reporting processes.

3. I collaborated with team members to develop a performance monitoring plan aimed at improving health service delivery outcomes.

4. I engaged in discussions with stakeholders to gather feedback on current evaluation practices and to explore opportunities for enhancing collaboration.

5. I assisted in the preparation of a report summarizing the findings from the recent health program evaluations, which will be presented to the management team.

6. I observed the implementation of data collection methods in the field, which provided practical insights into the challenges faced during the monitoring process.

7. I attended a workshop on networking and collaboration strategies, which emphasized the importance of building relationships with various health organizations.

8. I documented my experiences and reflections on the practical application of monitoring and evaluation theories learned in class.

This report encapsulates my key activities and learnings over the past week, contributing to my professional development in health systems management.

Field Practice Guideline for Undergraduate Students 1 A: Preamble

Mzumbe University, a prominent public institution in Tanzania, is
dedicated to facilitating the acquisition, development, preservation,
and dissemination of knowledge and skills through education, research,
and professional services. Mzumbe University was established by the
Mzumbe University Charter, 2007 under Section 25 of the Universities
Act. No. 7 of 2005 which repealed the Mzumbe University Act. No 9 of
2001. As a Training Institute, the University boasts over 50 years of
experience in training in the administration of justice, business
management, public administration, accountancy, finance, political
science, and good governance. The School of Public Administration and
Management (SOPAM) is one of the three largest academic units within the
University. The School has its academic departments, namely the
Department of Public Service and Human Resources Management, the
Department of Local Governance and Management Studies, and the
Department of Health Systems Management.

The Department of Health Systems Management hosts several academic
programs that include Bachelor of Health Systems Management, Bachelor of
Health Systems in Monitoring and Evaluation, Master of Health Systems
Management and Master of Science in Health Monitoring and Evaluation.
The Bachelor of Health Systems in Monitoring and Evaluation is the first
undergraduate degree program in Tanzania. The Department of Health
Systems has designed guidelines to help students during their field
practicals. The aim is to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge
and practical application, foster professional development, and ensure
ethical and effective M&E practices.

It corresponds to the needs and opportunities in social, economic and
technological development for the prosperity of individuals,

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 6

Department of Health Systems Management 2 B: Aims of the Field
Attachment for BHSME - Student

The Mzumbe university under the students' bylaws of 2023 recognizes the
importance of field attachment to every undergraduate student.

Therefore the primary goal of field attachment for BHSME students is to
enable them to translate the theories into practice to be able to
achieve intended better results that meet individual, organizational and
labor market demands from both local and international perspectives. The
goal is backed up with the following specific objectives: 1. To enable
students to experience how health organizations/institutions and
health-related ones capture monitoring and evaluation concepts in their
developmental interventions 2. To enable students to experience the
strengths and challenges of data management and data use in health
organizations/institutions and health- related ones 3. To enable
students, examine the levels of M&E capacity in health
organizations/institutions and health-related ones 4. To enable students
to understand the interlinkages and interconnectedness of policymakers
and implementers on the M&E concepts and frameworks in the health sector
5. To enable students to strengthen their skills and knowledge in M&E
research-based 6. To enable students to analyze and determine their
competence level and gaps in meeting labor market demands at both local
and international levels 7. To enable students to develop networking
with the real world while transforming ideas into realities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 7

Field Practice Guideline for Undergraduate Students 3 C: Duration of
Field Attachment

The field attachment for BHSME students will cover a total of seventeen
(17) weeks of the third year's first semester. D: Specific Areas where
Students can be Attached for Field Practices 1. Hospitals and healthcare
facilities with a wider range of services and programs 2. Ministry and
government departments dealing with planning, implementation and
evaluation of different development activities 3. Private/consulting
firms dealing with the design and implementation of research,
project/program, and M&E 4. Research and academic institutions with
research and M&E programs 5. Community health organizations implementing
different health-related interventions and programs 6. Health insurance
companies from both public and private 7. International development
organizations implementing different programs within or outside the
country 8. Global health organizations 9. Policy and advocacy
organization 10. Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) implementing
various projects and programs E: Competencies that Students should
Develop and Demonstrate

The student pursuing a Bachelor of Health Systems Management in
Monitoring and Evaluation should demonstrate competency and participate
to know how to effectively design, implement, and manage monitoring and
evaluation activities, ensuring that projects/programs or organization
achieve their intended outcomes and provide valuable insights for
continuous improvement.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 8

Department of Health Systems Management 4 F: Technical Competencies
Related to Monitoring and Evaluation 1.0 M&E Activities development and
organization settings 1.1 Students should be able to understand and
develop M&E activities 1.2 Students should be able to link the regular
organizational plan and its M&E plan 1.3 Students should understand the
budgeting of M&E activities 1.4 Developing innovative approaches to
improve M&E processes and overcome challenges that exist in the
organization 2.0 Data management and data use 2.1. Students should be
able to develop a clear understanding of various sources of data; Hard
documents eg (MTUHA Registers), surveys reports and soft wares such as
DHIS2, CTC3 Database, PlanRep, FFARS, MUSE, GoTHOMIS etc ( the
organization should not limit the student to only these tools instead
all available sources). 2.2. Students should be able to or engaged in
designing surveys, conducting interviews, focus groups, and using
statistical analysis tools. Also using other tools in data collection
like Kobo collect, Google Forms, e-dodoso etc. 2.3. Students should
develop expertise in using databases and data management software to
organize and retrieve data efficiently. 2.4. Students should be able to
understand planning and budgeting tools (software) available in the
organization not limited to; PlanRep. budgeting and expenditures
management tools (software)eg FFARS, MUSE, GoTHOMIS etc. 2.5. Students
should be acquainted with tools like SPSS, STATA, SAS, Excel or R or any
data analysis tools that are used by the host organization. 2.6.
Students be acquainted with the data use plan used by the host
organization -practices and pieces of evidence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 9

Field Practice Guideline for Undergraduate Students 5 2.7. Students
should be able to conduct the survey and use the findings for program
improvement. 2.8. Students should be able to understand how Surveillance
is done and use the findings. 2.9. Students should be able to conduct
data auditing. 2.10. Students should understand how supervision and
capacity building is done. 2.11. Students should be able to identify
various sources of knowledge within the organization (both Tacit and
Implicit) and use information (findings) resulting from M&E for
organizational learning. 2.12. Student should participate in leveraging
new technologies and tools to enhance data collection, analysis, and
reporting. 2.13. Students should participate in ensuring that all data
and analyses are accurate and reliable and carefully reviewing all
aspects of M&E processes to avoid errors and omissions. 3.0 M&E
Research: Evaluation Techniques 3.1. Students should develop and
practice understanding different types of evaluations and when to use
them. (Formative Evaluation (i.e.,. Process Evaluation & Summative
evaluation particularly Outcome and Impact Evaluation, Baseline Surveys,
Midterm Evaluation, End line Evaluation and Ex-post Evaluation) 3.2.
Students should be able to differentiate the purposes of formative,
process, and outcome evaluation and explain how findings from each are
used. 3.3. Students should be able to assess evaluation reports in
relation to their quality, utility, and impact on public health 3.4.
Students are expected to acquire and fully utilize skills in assessing
the direct and indirect effects of a program or intervention or any
activities performed by the organization in reflection with prior-
identified indicators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 10

Department of Health Systems Management 6 4.0 M&E Research: Performance
Monitoring 4.1. Students should participate in development and use SMART
(Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) indicators.
4.2. Students should develop and demonstrate Proficiency in frameworks
like Logical Framework Approach (LogFrame), Theory of Change (ToC), and
Results-Based Management (RBM) /Result Framework or any other frameworks
available in the organization 4.3. Students should participate in the
development of the Program/ Project Logic Model 4.4. Students should be
able to develop project/program targets such as baseline targets,
interim targets and final targets 4.5. Students should be able to
understand various program components including inputs, activities,
output, outcome and impacts 4.6. Students should be able to understand
the program theory and how to prepare the project/program Document 4.7.
Students should be able to apply various economic evaluation principles
while designing and selecting an intervention such as Cost Benefit
Analysis (CBA), Cost Utility Analysis (CUA), Cost Effectiveness Analysis
(CEA) and other principles. The host organization may not be limited to
the mentioned principles only 5.0 Networking and collaboration a.\
The students is expected to develop negotiation skills and effective
communication with project/ project stakeholders or members of the
organization, including donors, beneficiaries, and team members. b.\
Students should work collaboratively with project teams, including
contributing to team goals and supporting colleagues. Building strong
relationships and networks within and outside the organization. c.\
Students should understand the flow of information and communication
channels at different levels within and outside the organization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 11

Field Practice Guideline for Undergraduate Students 7 d.\
Students are expected to know how the partnership works in monitoring
and evaluation or the overall management of the project, program or
organization. G: Roles of the Host Organization (Employer) 1. To orient
students on various sections and units available in the organization
(organization structure and its scope of operation) 2. To assign a
student with the roles/activities/ tasks related to his/her profession
3. To oversee student's progress and give constructive feedback to
students for better improvement 4. To assist/coach student on assigned
duties/activities 5. To ensure a student adheres to professional ethical
conduct. 6. To sign and verify the student's logbook based on the
activities performed daily 7. Be able to respond to questions that will
be raised by the field supervisor from Mzumbe University during the
assessment (field visit) 8. Allow the student to conduct his/her
evaluation/research project after thoroughly reviewing the student's
evaluation proposal H: Roles of Student (Prospective Employee) 1. To
report at the station on time. 2. To accomplish all assigned activities.
3. To report any challenges observed upon fulfilling his/her duties and
responsibilities. 4. Be able to receive feedback from the host
supervisor and make sure he/she responds accordingly. 5. Be ready to
learn and cope with the organization's environment 6. Work in a team

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Page 12

Department of Health Systems Management 8 7. Adhere to the professional
ethical conduct of M&E 8. To prepare daily field reports (Logbook). 9.
Daily attendance register (to sign in and out). 10. To be creative and
innovative in solving daily situational problems. I:\
Roles of the Department (Mzumbe University) 1. To facilitate linkage
between the student and the host Organization 2. To make follow up on
the student's progress 3. To solve problems which may be encountered by
students during field time. 4. To provide physical field assessment to
both prospective employees (field student) and host supervisor 5.
Assigning a department/school member to oversee the student's fieldwork,
provide feedback and support 6. Evaluating student's performance during
the field placement and providing constructive feedback for improvement
7. To help students in accessing field placement by providing them with
field attachment letter in time. Note: The end product should be a field
report with enough details as per field objectives and their
corresponding competencies. This work has to be given the weight in
semester exam.
